subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A rack and pinion mechanism converts:
options: Linear motion into oscillating motion only
questions.explain: A rotating pinion gear meshes with a straight toothed rack to convert rotary motion into linear motion.

questions.q: Motion that moves back and forth in a straight line is called:
questions.explain: Reciprocating motion is repeated back-and-forth movement in a straight line, as seen in a piston or a sewing-machine needle.

questions.q: Soldering and brazing are both methods of:
options: Joining metals using a filler that melts at a lower temperature than the parts
Casting molten metal into a mould
questions.explain: Soldering and brazing join metal parts using a molten filler alloy that flows between them, without melting the base metals themselves.

questions.q: Which joining method gives a permanent fixing rather than a temporary one?
questions.explain: Welding fuses parts together permanently, whereas bolts, screws and press studs can be undone, making them temporary fixings.

questions.q: Developing a chosen idea differs from generating ideas because developing involves:
options: Refining and improving one concept by testing and modelling details
questions.explain: Development takes one promising idea and refines it through modelling, testing and detailing to improve it.

questions.q: Quality control during production is mainly carried out to:
options: Check products meet the specification and catch faults early
Increase the weight of every product
Make the product more expensive on purpose
questions.explain: Quality control involves checks and tests throughout production to ensure products meet the specification and to identify defects.

questions.q: A crank and slider mechanism converts:
options: Reciprocating motion into oscillating motion only
questions.explain: A crank and slider turns rotary motion into reciprocating (back-and-forth) linear motion, as in an engine.

questions.q: Freehand sketching is most useful in the design process for:
options: Quickly recording and developing initial ideas
Producing the final accurate manufacturing dimensions
questions.explain: Freehand sketching lets designers rapidly explore and communicate early ideas without the constraints of accurate measurement.

questions.q: A cam and follower mechanism is used to convert:
questions.explain: As a cam rotates, its profile pushes the follower up and down, converting rotary motion into reciprocating motion.

questions.q: A force that pulls or stretches a material is called:
questions.explain: Tension is a pulling or stretching force, while compression is a squashing force.

questions.q: In a gear train, an idler gear is added mainly to:
options: Change the overall gear ratio of the train
Reverse the direction of the output gear without changing the ratio
questions.explain: An idler gear sits between driver and driven gears to reverse the output's direction; it does not affect the overall gear ratio.

questions.q: User-centred design places the greatest emphasis on:
options: The needs, wants and abilities of the people who will use the product
questions.explain: User-centred design focuses on the end users' needs and limitations throughout the design process.

questions.q: A working drawing differs from a presentation drawing because it:
options: Uses bright realistic colours to impress a client
Provides accurate dimensions and details needed to manufacture the product
questions.explain: A working drawing contains the precise dimensions, materials and details a manufacturer needs to make the product accurately.

questions.q: In an isometric drawing, vertical lines stay vertical and the other edges are drawn at:
questions.explain: Isometric drawings keep verticals upright and draw receding edges at 30 degrees to the horizontal to give a 3D impression.

questions.q: Producing several different rough ideas before choosing one is part of which stage of the design process?
questions.explain: Generating ideas involves creating a range of possible solutions, often through sketching, before developing the best one.

questions.q: A CNC router is an example of:
options: CAM, where a computer controls the cutting machine
questions.explain: A CNC (computer numerical control) router is a CAM machine that cuts a workpiece automatically from a digital file.

questions.q: A design brief is best described as:
options: A list of every tool in the workshop
A short statement outlining the problem and what the design should achieve
questions.explain: A design brief is a concise statement that sets out the problem, the client's needs and what the design must accomplish.

questions.q: A 'former' (mould) is used in vacuum forming to:
options: Cut the finished part to size
Provide the shape the softened plastic is pulled over
questions.explain: In vacuum forming a heated plastic sheet is sucked down over a former, which gives the part its shape.

questions.q: Sand casting is a process in which:
options: Material is removed by a rotating cutter
Molten metal is poured into a sand mould and left to solidify
A sheet of plastic is bent over a former
questions.explain: In sand casting, molten metal is poured into a cavity formed in sand and allowed to cool and solidify into shape.

questions.q: A prototype is made primarily to:
options: Test and evaluate a design before final production
Sell directly to thousands of customers
questions.explain: A prototype is a working model used to test, evaluate and refine a design before committing to full production.

questions.q: A worm gear driving a worm wheel is often used because it:
options: Gives a large speed reduction and high torque in a compact space
questions.explain: A worm and wheel produces a large gear reduction, lowering speed and increasing torque in a small space.

questions.q: Ergonomics in product design is concerned mainly with:
options: How comfortable, efficient and easy a product is for people to use
The colour of the packaging only
The selling price of the product
questions.explain: Ergonomics focuses on designing products so they are comfortable, safe and efficient for people to interact with.
